title: Compact Card layer bleed & brand tinting strategy for console surfaces
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: Compact cards (summary tiles, mini-panels, KPI widgets) in the console show visual artifacts and inconsistent brand treatment in dark themes when we apply semi-opaque brand accent overlays and elevated glass-like surfaces. This leads to: inconsistent perceived elevation, brand accents that either 'wash out' or create high-contrast failures, and layout bleed issues where card edges visually clash with adjacent surfaces or charts inside the card.

Background: During the last theming pass we introduced a "brand tint" token used by prominent surface components. Cards are frequently used in compact density mode (8–12px padding) and often contain small tables, sparklines, and action buttons. In dark themes, the existing tint mapping (brand-300 @ 12% atop surface-800) produces either insufficient separation or violates contrast for small text/controls.

Goal: Define a token mapping and component override strategy for compact cards that: 1) preserves semantic elevation and focus hierarchy; 2) provides predictable, low-cost renderable overlays (avoid many layered alpha composites where possible); 3) keeps small copy, icons, and interactive controls meeting AA even when a brand tint is present; 4) provides a safe fallback for customer brand colors that are very saturated or low-luminance; 5) documents implementation patterns for components nested inside cards (tables, charts, buttons).

Scope: Compact card surfaces and their direct children (mini-tables, sparklines, action buttons, badges). This ticket is design work + handoff tokens and token-mapping guidance for engineering. Implementation and runtime optimizations will be tracked in ENG follow-ups.

Proposed approach (high level):
- Introduce two new semantic tokens: surface-card-bleed (for edge blend) and surface-card-overlay (for subtle tinting of content area). Both are semantic tokens that resolve differently per theme and per brand profile.
- For dark themes, use a multiply/lighten compositing approach only in our static token outputs: precompute brand-tint variants for the 12 most common brand palettes shipped by partners and for the platform brand. This avoids per-request compositing in the runtime where possible.
- Provide component overrides: compact-card border-radius/padding adjustments, separate background for inner content (surface-card-inner) to isolate charts/tables, and a clear rule that buttons inside compact-cards use button-surface-contrast token instead of inheriting the card tint.
- Accessibility safeguard: when brand-tint overlay reduces text contrast below AA for 12px UI text, automatically lower overlay opacity or shift to neutral elevation (no tint).

Deliverables:
- Finalized token names and resolved hex/alpha values for surface-card-bleed and surface-card-overlay for light/dark/brand variants.
- Component override spec for CompactCard, CompactTable (row/hover/bg rules), CompactSparkline (background and axis contrast), and SmallActionButton inside cards.
- Figma file with tokenized components and 6+ example brand integrations (including saturated red/blue/green brand cases).
- Handoff doc for ENG with explicit runtime fallback logic and KG cache-friendly recommendations.

Acceptance criteria:
- Compact card states (default, hover, focused, selected) are documented with token values and rendered in Figma for light + dark + 4 brand samples.
- Small text (12px/14px) and icons inside cards maintain AA contrast in all documented permutations or the spec includes an explicit fallback rule.
- A recommended mapping table exists: base token -> resolved theme value for surface-card-bleed and surface-card-overlay (six resolved values: light/default, light/brand, dark/default, dark/brand, dark/brand-fallback, high-contrast).
- Design sign-off from PM (Miguel Ortega) and Eng lead (Jia Chen) recorded in comments.

Constraints & known trade-offs:
- Precomputing brand variants increases token footprint but reduces per-request GPU work; engineering prefers this trade for hosted runtime.
- For very saturated brand colors, tinting can look muddy; we prefer desaturated-brand-overlay variants rather than pure alpha stacking in dark theme.
- Avoid adding new runtime CSS layering patterns that complicate mobile/web WebKit rendering; prefer single-layer backgrounds where feasible.
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototypes for compact-card in light + dark + 4 brand examples
Token mapping table exported to design-tokens spreadsheet with resolved hex/alpha values
Component overrides documented for CompactCard, CompactTable, CompactSparkline, SmallActionButton
Contrast check report showing AA compliance for 12/14px text or explicit fallback rules
Design sign-off from PM and Eng recorded in comments
design_decisions: Create two semantic tokens: surface-card-bleed (edge blend) and surface-card-overlay (content tint) to separate edge treatment from content area
Precompute brand-overlay variants for common partner palettes to avoid expensive runtime compositing
Prefer desaturated-brand-overlay in dark themes when brand luminance < 20% or saturation > 70%
Inner content (tables/charts) uses surface-card-inner with higher contrast; overlays should not apply to chart axes or small controls
Buttons inside compact cards must use button-surface-contrast token and not inherit card overlay to preserve CTA legibility
implementation_notes: Token names: surface-card-bleed, surface-card-overlay, surface-card-inner, brand-tint-weak, brand-tint-strong
Engineers: provide exported token JSON with 6 resolved variants per token (light/default, light/brand, dark/default, dark/brand, dark/brand-fallback, high-contrast)
Runtime hint: where possible, prefer single-layer BG images or flattened RGBA on server side for static dashboards to reduce WebGL/Canvas overdraw
Provide a small JS utility in the console theming lib: resolveCardOverlay(brand, theme, density) -> tokenName to centralize fallback logic
Avoid mixing overlay with drop shadows; keep elevation via subtle shadows and use overlay only for brand tinting
qa_checklist: Verify token exports match Figma hex/alpha values
Validate small text/icon contrast in all permutations using automated contrast tool
Test CompactCard with nested CompactTable: row hover and selected states must not inherit overlay opacity for cell text
Check sparklines inside cards on dark-brand variants for axis visibility and stroke legibility
Manual regression: legacy dashboards (top 20 by traffic) rendered in staging to catch unexpected bleed artifacts
